model_variants._note: Alternatives to CollisionFreeSpeed (model + agents above), used by validate_juelich.py --model. JuPedSim defaults unless noted.

social_force._force_note: JuPedSim defaults 120000/240000 push agents through walls under compression (crash within ~6 s at a 1 m bottleneck); 1/10 is stable
social_force._radius_note: JuPedSim default is 0.3 m; 0.25 m so people fit the 3/m² start lattice without overlapping

routing._note: one_way: inbound only through inbound_gates (gate_weights renormalised over them), outbound only through outbound_gates. The model fails two-way flow above ~2/m² (README, Validation), and one-way systems are standard at the Kumbh. two_way: the old set-up, every gate both ways.
routing._gates_note: G2's lane is the only link between the nose and the pontoons, so it carries outbound only; with G2 inbound, people heading for G0/G1 walked up it head-on (test 2026-11-01).
routing._bathing_note: Time between reaching the bathing goal and walking back out. A guess.

normal_day._outflow_note: Share of bathers who walk back out through the area after bathing_min; the rest leave by boat or another route. A guess.
normal_day._minutes_note: At 1000/min the area was still filling after 45 min (walk in ~15-25, bathe 10, walk out ~20).
normal_day.note: Ordinary snan day. Inflow at the nose is not known; swept over an assumed range.

mauni_amavasya.note: Main bathing day. Assumed range around and above the summed gate capacity (~3400/min at 1.3 people/m/s).

analysis._counterflow_note: A cell is counter-flow when the smaller direction is at least min_share of its people; at or above counterflow_ppm2 the model is not validated there (Jülich two-way replay).

pings._note: Phase 4: synthetic phone pings drawn from simulated people. Values fixed before looking at results.
pings._sigma_note: Standard deviation per axis. Phone GPS is ~5 m in the open, worse near buildings and in dense crowds.

warning._alarm_density_note: Fruin level of service F for walkways (under 0.5 m² per person) starts at 2/m².
warning._alarm_speed_note: Weidmann's speed-density relation gives 0.5 m/s at about 2.3/m².
warning._event_note: Danger event: a 4 m cell at or above analysis.dense_ppm2 for event_hold_s in a row. Its zone's onset is what a warning must beat.
warning._min_zone_note: Zones with less walkable ground are slivers of road at a zone corner; a few GPS points snapped into them look like a crowd (found 2026-11-02). Their cells still count for the neighbouring zones.

go._note: Set 2026-11-02 before testing the rules: at 2% phones (15 s, 10 m), median density error <= 30%, first jam warned >= lead_min ahead in >= lead_ok_share of draws, and on a calm day at most false_alarms_per_hour alarmed zones per hour (median).

rules._note: Variants tested in rules.py; chosen on oneway_in1000 + calm_in500, then checked on holdout_jam + holdout_calm.
rules._neighbour_note: true: at least one of the 8 neighbouring zones meets the same condition at the same time.
rules._slow_note: 0.8: also require the median phone speed over the zone and its neighbours below 0.8 m/s (Weidmann: about 1.5/m²).

flow._note: flow.py: phones entering minus leaving a zone and its 8 neighbours. Alarm when the surplus is beyond chance (in - out >= sigmas * sqrt(in + out)), at that rate the block would reach dense_ppm2 within forecast_min, and both have held hold_s. A phone's first ping counts as entering, and its track ending as leaving (bathers leave the simulation at the goal).

bottleneck._note: bottleneck.py: phones passing counting circles on the roads that feed a known bottleneck give the demand (unique phones per window / share); alarm when demand exceeds the bottleneck's capacity by sigmas standard errors for hold_s. Bottlenecks come from the map (roads joining into a narrower one), not from simulation results.

sites.name: G3+G4 merge
sites._note: The G3 and G4 roads (5.5 m each) join into one 5.5 m road. Counting circles either 60 m up each road (near) or 30 m inside the G3 and G4 gates (gates, ~500 m and ~6 min walk upstream). The walk is real warning time: people counted at a gate reach the merge minutes later.

two_level._note: two_level.py: the bottleneck rule with a capacity the phones learn (calibrate.py) and two alerts. Amber: demand >= amber_frac x capacity; red: demand >= capacity; both by sigmas standard errors, held hold_s. Days are scored by what happened at the merge (20 m zones around it, 60 s): jam (>= 4/m² event), busy (peak >= busy_ppm2 but no jam: amber is right, red is false) or calm (both false). Settings chosen on the history runs, tested unchanged on unseen runs.
two_level._busy_note: Fruin level of service F for walkways (as alarm_density_ppm2); set before the test.

go._note: At 2% phones, set before the test. Jam days: first alert >= lead_min ahead in lead_ok_share of draws and red before the jam in red_before_jam_share. Days without a jam: red in at most false_red_share of draws. Calm days: amber in at most false_amber_calm_share.
